public584.matching_and_emission: PC run-one parser with a 32769-entry last-position hash table keyed from 4 input bytes; it probes the current position and lazy lookahead under the supplied skip=6/lazy=16 settings, folds prior tokens, and emits through the PC put-match path without ETINY's restricted allowed-length piece mask. This is a distinct parser engine path, not just a different routing constant.

public595_and_combo.matching_and_emission: ETINY builds a 4096-slot one-way table from 4-byte hashes, performs candidate lookups on an approximately 8-byte stride (q starts at 7 and advances by 8 on misses), verifies and extends matches in 8-byte steps, folds earlier tokens up to 16, and emits pieces limited by the length-code mask. A residual too short for any allowed piece remains literal/pending. Combo uses the same tiny-config output bytes and token hashes as public595.

r25_tiny_tail.new_component: et_piece_tail is called by et_cover and et_pieces. If the greedy allowed piece would strand a remainder shorter than minl, it tests a two-piece split from already-allowed lengths and chooses it only when both pieces are valid, more bytes are covered, and the estimated pc_gain sum beats the greedy piece.
r25_tiny_tail.model_scope: span 0..2048 and the recorded finite distance sample; not a Rust/Lean gate or a time measurement

dispatch_and_engine.mechanism_conclusion: The 8-byte R25 gain is from a match-piece segmentation repair inside the existing ETINY engine, not a route-constant edit. Public584 is a much larger alternate PC engine path with a different table/probe/lazy strategy and full-length emission; porting it is a separate engine migration, not the tiny-tail component.

round24_tiny_negative.mechanism: R24 tiny-converge stops SFtinytokens after a deterministic non-improving reassignment trial while retaining every improving iteration. The public-config file at 12000 bytes records 0 rounds/calls; tiny-app.log at 28000 bytes records 2 rounds, 1 improving round, and 0 rejected trials with a remaining round. The measured public workload therefore had no early-stop opportunity; this does not test ETINY allowed-length tail segmentation.
round24_tiny_negative.scope_note: The linked R18 exact-price DP repeat check was a separate Z308 dynamic-programming cache path and is not the ETINY tail-split mechanism either.

standard_total_time.interpretation: The raw original-encoder quality receipt has bytes and hashes, not repeated total compression times. Existing combo/#595 time JSONLs cannot identify tiny-tail's incremental cost because the tiny-tail source is not a measured method in those runs. Do not transfer time from another runner, batch, or source.

decision.reason: The repair has an actual original-encoder 8-byte/22-token result on the target file and changes only that file in the saved quality comparison. The direct time cost remains unknown. Eight bytes corresponds to only 0.0023809524 percentage points on the 28-file equal-weight axis, so this supports at most a paired combo-versus-tiny-tail standard screen before any full gate allocation.
decision.alternate_public584_path: A 332-byte size advantage over combo is recorded for the same file, but it comes from a different parser engine. Its time and port/proof cost are unknown and should be assessed as a separate route, not credited to tiny-tail.

limits: The byte comparison is for the fixed public 28-file encoder path and does not establish held-out stage2 performance.
The finite selector model does not replace native correctness or an original full gate.
No new standard timing, cross-runner comparison, implementation, or CI action was performed in this audit.
